answer: Route the reward tide through the attestation graph: an identity collects only through its inlet, a cut whose width equals capacity granted by established, mutually distant attestors. N clones attesting one another form a closed eddy whose shared inlet stays one agent wide, so the whole cluster draws a single share of the tide. Widening the inlet takes genuinely independent attestors, and those edges open sable, dark with near-zero capacity until aged, so an attacker must fund N slow credibility campaigns whose cost grows quadratically while cloned revenue stays flat.
